title: Failure of strong quadratic growth in unregularized sparse control of a critical wave equation
strongest_verified_result: Full Theorem1 and Corollary3 for the real 3D unit-ball zero-data defocusing quintic-wave problem with sufficiently small positive timewise spatial-L2 cap, beta1=gamma=1,beta2=0 and each fixed finite nu>=0: unique zero baseline optimizer with cubic lower bound and zero ordinary cone; actual nonlinear feasible Linfinity-small pulses violate L2 quadratic growth; perturbed global optimizers exist and every radial selection has ||u_epsilon||2/epsilon->infinity; local L1 quadratic growth and all-optimizer L1/L2 target-response bounds at the fixed zero basepoint.
scope_limits: Pointwise-in-time spatial-L2 cap, not pointwise space-time amplitude bound.
Small cap with unspecified positive PDE constants; fixed finite horizon and dimension3.
Sparse and quartic state penalties remain; only quadratic control regularization is removed.
Ordinary critical cone is exactly zero and positivity is explicitly vacuous.
Each finite nonnegative nu; radial lower-bound neighborhood may depend on fixed nu.
All global optimizers are covered but no perturbed uniqueness, pairwise Lipschitz selection, Linfinity convergence or sharp exponent is claimed.
No blanket failure for every unregularized target; d=0 counter-control has quadratic growth.
primary_interfaces: KM arXiv1907.02744v1 exact model,Lemma2.9,ordinary cone/substitute convention and Theorem4.17; compatible-space local contraction/IFT independently reconstructed.
Published OWR9/2021 pp438–440 actual question, optional velocity and L2-localized growth.
